'''{{lang|vi|Bún bò Huế}}''' (pronounced {{IPA|vi|ɓun˧˥ ɓɔ˧˩ hwe˧˥|}}) or '''{{lang|vi|bún bò}}''' ({{IPAc-en|lang|b|uː|n|_|b|ɔː}}) is a Vietnamese rice noodle ({{lang|vi|bún}}) dish with sliced beef ({{lang|vi|bò}}), {{lang|vi|[[chả lụa]]}}, and sometimes [[pork knuckle]]s.<ref name=kim/> The dish originates from [[Huế]], a city in central Vietnam associated with the cooking style of the former royal court.<ref>[[Thanh Nien Weekly]] 2 Dec 2011 print edition [http://www.thanhniennews.com/2010/pages/20111201-eating-hue-foods-as-locals.aspx When in Hue] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191017213753/http://www.thanhniennews.com/travel/when-in-hue-9348.html |date=2019-10-17 }} "The most popular Hue dish would have to be bún bò Huế, a spicy beef and vermicelli soup that goes down well with Vietnamese people and foreigners alike."</ref> The dish has a mix of spicy, salty, and savory flavors. The predominant flavors are those of [[Cymbopogon|lemongrass]] and [[shrimp paste]].<ref name=Thaker/> Compared to {{lang|vi|[[pho|phở]]}} or {{lang|vi|[[bún riêu]]}}, the noodles are thicker and cylindrical.<ref name=Danh/>
